argument:
The bull's RM338.918m sensitivity after mechanically removing inventory release shows meaningful cash survives a conservative adjustment. That answers a claim that recovery resources vanish without working-capital support. It is not a recurring forecast, and even the unadjusted RM462.958m surplus fell short of RM511.784m dividends.

At 17.71x earnings and 5.32% reported yield, cash-positive recovery offers potential compensation, but current distribution and expense trends weaken it. Quarterly profit/revenue fell from 13.06% to 10.69%; broadly flat H1 operating profit does not demonstrate margin repair. Lease-inclusive net debt of RM1.411bn makes cash retention relevant. A purchase requires confidence in cost normalisation or payout restraint, whereas neither is yet observed. I oppose treating the yield as fully cash-covered, while accepting that financing capacity makes recovery plausible.
key_points: Positive cash persists after the inventory sensitivity.
Current payout exceeds conservative cash coverage.
Margin repair or payout restraint must support the income case.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers whether some recovery funding remains, but its sensitivity strengthens rather than resolves the dividend-coverage shortfall. Cash-positive operations preserve upside; observed margin and payout pressure still qualify the quoted income return.
